title: Given an array that may contain duplicates, return all unique subsets using backtracking.
shortTitle: Subsets II (with duplicates) — sort then skip duplicates

s1_definition.profdef: Sort the array so equal values are adjacent, then run the standard subsets backtracking with one extra guard: within a single recursion level, skip an element if it equals the previous element already considered at that level (i > start and nums[i] == nums[i-1]). This suppresses duplicate subsets while still allowing a repeated value to be used deeper in the path.
s1_definition.analogy: National Bank of India has add-on vouchers where some are identical. Two identical vouchers should not produce two different-looking-but-equal packages. By lining up identical vouchers and, at each decision point, using an identical voucher only once as the "first" choice, you avoid listing the same package twice.
s1_definition.oneliner: Sort, then at each level skip a value equal to its predecessor to drop duplicate subsets.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** Sort the array so equal values are adjacent, then run the standard subsets backtracking with one extra guard: within a single recursion level, skip an element if it equals the previous element already considered at that level (i > start and nums[i] == nums[i-1]). This suppresses duplicate subsets while still allowing a repeated value to be used deeper in the path.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** National Bank of India has add-on vouchers where some are identical. Two identical vouchers should not produce two different-looking-but-equal packages. By lining up identical vouchers and, at each decision point, using an identical voucher only once as the "first" choice, you avoid listing the same package twice.

**One line to remember:** Sort, then at each level skip a value equal to its predecessor to drop duplicate subsets.

sections.s2_technical:
Sort first so duplicates sit together. In the loop, record the path at entry as usual, but skip when the current index is beyond the level's start and equals the previous value. For example: `if (i > start && nums[i] == nums[i-1]) continue;`.

The condition `i > start` is crucial: it allows the first occurrence at a level to be chosen (and recursed, where the duplicate can legitimately extend the path) but blocks a second identical choice at the same level, which would create a duplicate subset.

The time remains O(n · 2^n) in the worst case of all-distinct elements, less when duplicates prune branches. A senior nuance is that the same skip pattern reappears in Combination Sum II and Permutations II, so recognizing it as the general "skip same-level duplicates" idiom saves re-deriving it each time.
sections.s3_banking:
Problem 1 — At National Bank of India, a promotional bundle draws from a voucher pool that contains duplicate vouchers, and marketing wants every distinct bundle with no repeats in the list. This is exactly how unique subsets with duplicates works.

Problem 2 — Two identical vouchers must not yield two identical-looking bundles. This is exactly why the array is sorted and same-level duplicates are skipped.

The mini-project builds a `VoucherBundleGenerator`, a `BankLogFormatter`, and a runnable demo.

sections.s5_journey:
The input vouchers two, one, two are sorted to one, two, two.

Step 1: Entry records the empty bundle.

Step 2: Choosing the one records [1], then the first two records [1,2], then the second two records [1,2,2].

Step 3: Back at the top level, choosing the first two records [2] and [2,2].

Step 4: At the top level the second two is skipped because it equals its predecessor and i is beyond start, preventing a duplicate [2].

Step 5: The six unique bundles are produced with no repeats.

2026-10-26T23:50:00Z [INFO] Bundle: [1, 2]
2026-10-26T23:50:00Z [INFO] Bundle: [1, 2, 2]
2026-10-26T23:50:00Z [INFO] Bundle: [2]
2026-10-26T23:50:00Z [INFO] Bundle: [2, 2]

sections.s5b_flow:
```text
  sort [2,1,2] → [1,2,2]
  backtrack with guard  i>start && nums[i]==nums[i-1] → skip
    [] [1] [1,2] [1,2,2] [2] [2,2]
    second top-level 2 skipped (would duplicate [2])
  unique subsets = 6
```

sections.s6_takeaway:
Subsets II extends the power-set backtracking to inputs that contain duplicates, where the goal is every distinct subset with no repeats in the output. The two essential moves are sorting the array first so equal values are adjacent, and then adding a guard inside the loop that skips an element when its index is beyond the current level's start and it equals the previous element. That single condition suppresses duplicate subsets at each decision level.

The condition "index greater than start" is what makes it correct: the first occurrence of a duplicate value at a level is allowed and recursed into, where the duplicate can legitimately extend the path deeper, but a second identical choice at the same level is blocked because it would produce an already-generated subset. The worst-case cost is still O(n times 2 to the n).

In my project at National Bank of India, marketing built promotional bundles from a voucher pool that contained identical vouchers and needed every distinct bundle listed once. This sorted, skip-same-level-duplicate pattern produced clean unique bundles, and I always point out that the exact same idiom reappears in Combination Sum II and Permutations II, so I treat it as one reusable technique rather than three separate tricks.
